text:
Predicates:
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
Schedule(x) ::: x schedules a meeting with their customers.
GoToday(x) ::: x will go to the company building today.
LunchBuilding(x) ::: x has lunch in the company building.
LunchHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
Remote(x) ::: x is working remotely from home.
OtherCountries(x) ::: x is in other countries.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
Premises:
∀x ((Employee(x) ∧ Schedule(x)) → GoToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will go to the company building today.
∀x (LunchBuilding(x) → Schedule(x)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company building schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Employee(x) → (LunchBuilding(x) ⊕ LunchHome(x))) ::: Employees have lunch either in the company building or at home.
∀x (LunchHome(x) → Remote(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, they are working remotely from home.
∀x (OtherCountries(x) → Remote(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬Remote(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
GoToday(james) ↔ Manager(james) ::: James will appear in the company today if and only if he is a manager.
Conclusion:
(Manager(james) ∨ OtherCountries(james)) → ¬(LunchHome(james) ∨ Remote(james)) ::: If James is either a manager or in other countries, then James does not either have lunch at home or work remotely from home.
(LunchHome(james) ∨ Remote(james)) → (¬Manager(james) ∧ ¬OtherCountries(james)) ::: If James either has lunch at home or works remotely from home, then he is neither a manager nor does he work in other countries.
